transcript.speaker: Finnegan O'Malley
transcript.content: Emily, thanks for checking in — I appreciate it. I’m sorry I drifted during class; the virtual format just flattens things for me and I lose focus. I’m trying a few fixes: keeping my camera on, doing quick sketched notes during lectures, using 25-minute focus timers with short breaks, and asking a question at the start to stay involved. Do you have any other ideas—maybe something tactile or an accountability trick that might help me stay present?

transcript.speaker: Emily Harrison
transcript.content: Those are really solid changes — nice work. For something tactile, try a small textured object (a smooth stone, fidget ring, or stress ball) to handle when attention drifts, and keep a physical sketchbook or a strip of sticky notes where you jot one key phrase every 10–15 minutes. For accountability, pair up with a classmate to swap a one-sentence takeaway after each session or post a brief goal in chat at the start and one-line reflection at the end — small public commitments are surprisingly effective. If you want, I can check in after a few classes and we can tweak what’s working.
